issues.title: Out-of-domain class-K evaluation in the invariance proof
issues.failure_explanation: The function m is declared only on [0,nu]. From delta-h alpha M(delta)^2 <= delta' and delta'>=0, it does not follow that delta-h alpha M(delta)^2 is nonnegative. Nevertheless, eq:delta_prime_ub1 applies m to that expression and the next equation asserts the resulting bound for all delta in [0,epsilon]. The later high-sublevel case does establish a positive lower bound, but only after the universal equation has already been stated; the low-sublevel case does not need that equation at all.
issues.overall_effect: A displayed bound used in the proof is undefined over part of its asserted range, though the theorem can be recovered by a local reordering of the two-case argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Split the proof into the cases δ≤ε/2 and δ>ε/2 before invoking m. In the low-sublevel case, use only δ′≤δ and the Taylor estimate. In the high-sublevel case, first choose h so that δ′≥δ−hαM(δ)^2>ε/4, and then use m(δ′)≥m(ε/4) in the upper bound for δ′. Delete the universal evaluation of m at the potentially negative quantity δ−hαM(δ)^2.
issues.why_classification: The out-of-domain evaluation is a genuine proof error rather than a transcriptional typo. Nevertheless, the old proof already contains the positivity estimate needed in the only case where the dissipative bound is used. Reordering those existing steps is short and routine and preserves the theorem without any new lemma or weakening.

issues.title: Taylor-segment domain in the positive-invariance proof
issues.failure_explanation: The exact endpoint lies in U^epsilon and the numerical endpoint is close to it, but membership of the endpoints in sublevel sets does not imply that their straight segment lies in U, which need not be convex. Since V and its Hessian are defined only on U, the Taylor expansion and uniform Hessian remainder in eq:V_taylor1 require a neighborhood/segment argument that is absent in the old proof. The symbol c used for the numerical endpoint is also not fixed there.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the general one-step positive-invariance theorem has not justified its local Taylor estimate, although the theorem is recoverable under the existing assumptions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use compact containment of U^ε in the open set U to choose r>0 with the closed r-neighborhood of U^ε contained in U. Uniform local truncation error makes the numerical endpoint lie within r of the exact endpoint for sufficiently small h; the joining segment is then contained in that neighborhood. Bound the gradient and Hessian there, define or eliminate the unused constant c, and apply Taylor's theorem on the justified segment.
issues.why_classification: Endpoint membership does not itself justify Taylor expansion on a nonconvex domain, so mathematical checking is required. The missing check is, however, a standard compact-neighborhood argument under the existing assumptions and changes neither the statement nor its guarantees. It is a short local repair.

issues.title: Manifold-restricted sublevel invalidates the scaled-gain theorem
issues.failure_explanation: In the old definition, U^epsilon contains only points on M, whereas U^epsilon_{h,beta/h} contains Euclidean Euler segments. No assumption makes those segments remain on M. For example, take U=R^2, M={(s,0)}, f=0, and V(s,t)=(s+t)^2+t^2. These data satisfy the eligibility conditions, but at (a,0) the gradient is (2a,2a), so every nontrivial scaled-gradient segment immediately leaves M. Hence the claimed inclusion fails literally and cannot imply positive invariance of the ambient set V^{-1}([0,epsilon]). The adaptive proofs likewise use bounds over U^epsilon after their iterates may have left M.
issues.overall_effect: The literal scaled-gain segment inclusion is false, and the later adaptive proofs lack bounds on the ambient points actually generated by their updates.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In def:01, replace U^ε={x∈M:V(x)≤ε} by the ambient sublevel U^ε=V^{-1}([0,ε])⊂U. Consequently, interpret L and all sublevel-based bounds in thm:optimal_a, thm:adaptive_a, and thm:adaptive_a_period over that ambient sublevel; no projection or additional manifold-invariance premise is needed.
issues.why_classification: The ambient reading is uniquely forced by the old source itself: U^ε is called a sublevel set, the preceding invariance result concerns V^{-1}([0,ε]), the theorem immediately claims that its inclusion implies invariance of that ambient set, and the Euler segments and adaptive iterates are ambient. No argument uses the manifold-restricted meaning. The extraneous x∈M qualifier is therefore a transcriptional definition error, not a missing mathematical construction or an intended exact-manifold guarantee.

issues.title: Full-segment inclusion for scaled gains
issues.failure_explanation: Under the intended ambient interpretation of U^epsilon, eq:V_segment2 places each segment only in U^{epsilon+Delta}. The subsequent two-case argument uses eq:V_segment4 at t=1 to prove V(x_{k+1})<=epsilon. Endpoint invariance does not by itself imply that every intermediate point has V<=epsilon, so the proof supports a weaker conclusion than U^epsilon_{h,beta/h} subset U^epsilon. Consequently, the asserted identity L(h,alpha)=L and demonstrated admissibility of the Taylor-bound minimizer are not established by the old proof.
issues.overall_effect: The stronger segment invariant and the resulting identification of the Hessian bound are unsupported, although the endpoint positive-invariance estimate remains available and is sufficient for later uses needing only that weaker conclusion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: After establishing S_k⊂U^{ε+Δ}, retain the parameter t in eq:V_segment1. If V(x_k)≤ε/2, its right-hand side is at most ε/2+c_β^2h^2 for every t∈[0,1]. If V(x_k)>ε/2, use the Łojasiewicz bound and t^2≤t to obtain V(x_k+t(x_{k+1}−x_k))≤ε−t[c_β^1(ε/2)^{2θ}−c_β^2h^2]. Choosing h by the corresponding existing thresholds proves S_k⊂U^ε, and hence restores L(h,β/h)=L and admissibility of β=1/L.
issues.why_classification: The endpoint argument does not imply the asserted full-segment inclusion, so this is not a typo. However, the old proof already supplies the required t-dependent Taylor inequality and all uniform constants. Applying the same two cases uniformly in t is a short, routine extension that preserves the full theorem and its optimal-gain conclusion.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: We now prove the stronger inclusion $S_k\subset U^\varepsilon$.

issues.title: Adaptive Hessian estimate used before tube-domain inclusion

failure_location.quote: From the update~\eqref{eq:adaptive_feedback1}, it is easy to see that

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem assumes that the Hessian is Gamma-Lipschitz only on the stated sublevel domain, while the proof estimates every point of U_{h,x_k,beta_k} without first placing that set there. In particular, the tube may contain points outside the assumed Lipschitz domain, and x_k may lie in the zero set excluded by V^{-1}(0,nu). Thus the estimate used to prove U_{h,x_k,beta(x_k)} subset K_{x_k} is not justified. The periodic theorem repeats the same domain-sensitive construction.
issues.overall_effect: The stepwise adaptive boundedness theorem, and the periodic theorem insofar as it inherits the same local Hessian argument, lack an established uniform one-step estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Before applying a Hessian Lipschitz estimate, choose a reduced level η<ε and r>0 such that the r-neighborhood of U^η lies in U^ν. Shrink η and h so that hF_η+M(η)/(cH_min)≤r. Then every z∈U_{h,x,β(x)} satisfies |z−x|≤hF_η+M(η)/(cH_min) and therefore lies in the domain where the C^3 regularity supplies a uniform Hessian Lipschitz bound, including at V=0. Use this bound to prove the K_x inclusion, and insert the same preliminary containment or first-exit check in each periodic-update block.
issues.why_classification: The old estimate is applied before its domain hypotheses are verified, but the missing verification follows routinely from compact containment, C^3 regularity, H_min>0, and M(η)→0. The same local check propagates to the periodic theorem without changing either algorithm, conclusion, or substantive assumptions. No new nontrivial lemma or proof architecture is required.

issues.title: Uniform scaling for periodically updated adaptive gains
issues.failure_explanation: Equation eq:tube-final contains a factor of order T_update/h multiplying the fixed-level gradient bound. For a fixed positive level this grows without bound as h tends to zero. Moreover, h_0(eta)=O(eta^theta) is only an upper bound and does not imply that eta^q/h_0(eta) is bounded when q=theta; a threshold of smaller order would satisfy the stated big-O relation while making the ratio diverge. Setting h equal to one particular half-threshold and then informally shrinking the level does not prove the required result for every h below one common h_0.
issues.overall_effect: The old argument does not establish the claimed all-time boundedness uniformly for every sufficiently small step size under a fixed physical gain-update period.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Derive from the explicit one-step thresholds a lower bound of the form h̄_0(η)≥C_hη^q for all sufficiently small η; this follows from q=θ≥1/2 and the minimum of the η^{1/2} and η^θ thresholds. For each arbitrary sufficiently small h, choose η=(2h/C_h)^{1/q}. Then h<h̄_0(η) and M(η)≤C_Mη^q=O(h), so with n=⌈T_update/h⌉ the accumulated block displacement is bounded by (T_update+h) times an h-independent constant. Choose T_update and a common h_0 to satisfy the geometric and Hessian margins, and close the argument by induction over update blocks.
issues.why_classification: The old big-O assertion has the wrong logical direction for the needed ratio, and checking one selected half-threshold does not establish the universal quantifier over all smaller h. Recovering the theorem requires a nontrivial coupling of the invariant level to h and a uniform block estimate. This is a contained scaling reconstruction that preserves the same assumptions and all-time boundedness guarantee, so it exceeds a minor repair but does not require global proof architecture or mathematical loss.
